title: Satellite Prefetch & Progressive Output PRD (SDK + Tooling) - WIP
content:
Context:
This is a working PRD sketch proposing a combined approach for: compact streaming, progressive-fidelity outputs, and tool-call prefetching targeted at intermittent-connectivity clients (mobile, satellite links, embedded devices). Goal is to enable low-bandwidth clients to remain responsive while preserving eventual full-fidelity results and correct tool-call semantics.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Many customers embed Redwood-hosted API calls in mobile apps, field devices, and low-bandwidth environments. Current streaming model assumes continuous connectivity and low network variance.
- When connectivity is poor the UX either stalls waiting for full results or degrades by showing partial/gibberish.
- Tool calls (external APIs, DB lookups, code execution) are particularly painful: latency spikes can block a session and cause retry complexity on client.
- SDK ergonomics for these clients are underdeveloped: no compact replay tokens, no formal progressive-fidelity negotiation, no first-class prefetch for declared tool outputs.

Proposal overview (high level):
1) Progressive-fidelity output layers
   - Response layers: SUMMARY (very compact), DELTA (incremental text / structured fields), FULL (complete structured output).
   - Server streams SUMMARY immediately (<= 280 chars) where available; client displays optimistic placeholder.
   - DELTA frames stream next (compact diffs/attachments). FULL delivered when connectivity allows or via background fetch.
   - Each layer carries an integrity token (hash) and monotonic sequence id so client can verify and reconcile.

2) Satellite-prefetch tool-call contracts
   - Allow model prompts to declare tool-call intents and the expected shape of tool outputs (schema).
   - Redwood will optionally (policy controlled by customer) prefetch tool-call results for declared tools and attach lightweight stubs to SUMMARY (e.g., cached/approx result, ttl, confidence).
   - Prefetch priorities: local cache -> best-effort remote -> deferred-execute (when client regains connectivity).

3) Compact replay tokens and micropatch frames
   - Each streamed fragment includes a compact replay token which encodes: session id, last-ack-seq, and minimal state to resume or request missing fragments from the server.
   - Micropatch frames represent small deterministic state changes (e.g., field x changed: value->value2) rather than resending entire JSON.

4) SDK ergonomics (patterns for client engineers)
   - High-level SDK surface: call.startStreaming({ prompt, tool_hints, fidelity: "auto|summary|full", resumeToken?: string }) -> returns a StreamingSession object.
   - StreamingSession.on('summary', fn), .on('delta', fn), .on('tool_stub', fn), .on('complete', fn), .resume(token)
   - Built-in helpers: presentOptimisticCard(summary), applyMicropatches(obj, patches), verifyIntegrity(token, expectedHash).
   - Mobile default: fidelity:auto, show summary immediately, queue background full fetch with exponential backoff.

5) Backward compatibility / fallbacks
   - Non-upgraded clients continue to receive full stream as today. Server will emit SUMMARY + DELTA + FULL if client advertises support; otherwise unchanged wire.
   - For critical tool calls annotated with must_execute=true, Redwood will allocate execution capacity in fast-path; otherwise prefetch may be best-effort.

Wire-level sketch (protocol notes):
- New frame types: SUMMARY_FRAME, DELTA_FRAME, PATCH_FRAME, TOOL_STUB_FRAME, REPLAY_TOKEN_FRAME, END_FRAME
- Each frame: { frame_type, seq, session_id, timestamp, payload_base64_or_json, integrity_hash }
- Replay token: base64(session_id|last_seq|short_mac) designed to be <= 64 bytes

Server-side behaviors and routing:
- Smart routing decision whether to prefetch tools depends on: customer policy, historical latency to tool endpoint, budget tag, and model prompt sensitivity.
- Prefetch costs charged to the customer but flagged as prefetch; visible in Console billing tab.

Observability and metrics (Console + telemetry):
- New telemetry events: summary_emitted, delta_rate, prefetch_attempt, prefetch_hit, prefetch_miss, replay_requests, patch_apply_failures.
- KPI targets (example): 90th percentile summary-to-first-delta <= 120ms for hosted-api, prefetch success rate >= 75% for declared low-latency tools in sample workload.

Security and privacy notes:
- Tool stubs may contain sensitive info; stubbing respects customer masking rules and redaction policies.
- Replay tokens should not contain PII; they are MACed and ephemeral.

Client UX flows (examples):
1) Mobile chat with intermittent network
   - User sends prompt. Server returns SUMMARY frame in <100ms: "Proposed plan: 3 step checklist" + small tool_stub for calendar query showing availability window. Client shows optimistic card.
   - As network persists, DELTA frames fill in details and micropatches refine structured checklist. If connection drops, client persists replay token and later resumes to fetch missing patches.

2) Field device (satellite) doing legal doc synthesis + lookup
   - Prompt declares a citation_tool expected to return 1-3 items. Server prefetches common citation hits and attaches tool_stub with confidence. Client displays placeholders; when full tool call arrives (hours later) the UI reconciles by applying patches and showing provenance.

Open questions / risks:
- Cost model: customers may abuse prefetch to run expensive tool calls. Need tractable limits and clear billing UX.
- Consistency semantics: how to present eventual changes to users in a predictable way (non-surprising updates).
- Tool idempotency: prefetch may cause side-effects unless tools are annotated read-only. Must define tool contract.
- Cache staleness and TTL heuristics for stubs.

Implementation roadmap (phases):
Phase 0 (experiment):
- Implement SUMMARY frame + replay token + client SDK hooks for summary/delta. Server: simple heuristic to emit summary for long responses (model abstraction).
- Console: telemetry + prefetch trial metrics.

Phase 1 (prefetch opt-in):
- Tool-hints in prompt schema; small prefetch service that can call declared tool endpoints with budget guardrails.
- SDK: resume tokens + micropatch apply library for JS/Android/iOS minimal API.

Phase 2 (policy + billing + rollout):
- Prefetch policy controls in Console (per-workspace, per-route).
- Billing flags for prefetch; SLO definitions for must_execute vs best-effort.

Acceptance criteria (early):
- SDKs can display summary within 200ms in 95% of sample mobile requests.
- Background resume fetch completes to FULL within 2x baseline latency in stable networks.
- Prefetch errors are surfaced as tool_stub with confidence=false rather than blocking main response.

Testing / QA plan:
- Simulate packet-loss and high-latency networks in test harness, verify resume behavior and micropatch reconciliation.
- Tool prefetch fuzz tests to ensure idempotency annotations are respected.
- Load tests to measure added memory/CPU from storing replay tokens and patch deltas per session.

Developer notes / next steps:
- Assign owners: eng-serving-runtime (Tomoko) for frame-level support; developer-experience (Ethan) for SDK shapes; product-hosted-api (Aisha) for Console policy UI.
- Create JIRA epic JIRA-PI-332 and link implementation PRs.
- Write short prototype RFC for wire frames and include sample JS SDK snippet for feedback.

Appendix: sample SDK snippet (pseudocode)
- call.startStreaming({prompt, tool_hints:[{name:\"calendar\",schema:\"{start,end}\"}], fidelity:'auto'})
- session.on('summary', s => showCard(s.text, s.tool_stubs))
- session.on('delta', d => applyMicropatches(doc, d.patches))
- session.on('complete', () => fetchFullIfMissing(session.replayToken))

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally exploratory. Looking for feedback on: what tool contracts we need, acceptable billing guardrails for prefetch, and how conservative to be with making prefetch the default.

Unresolved action items:
- [ ] Define exact replay token crypto spec (short MAC algorithm).
- [ ] Decide default fidelity for mobile SDKs (opt-in vs opt-out).
- [ ] Draft Console UI copy for prefetch billing flag.
